title: Finite type algebras over arbitrary domains are generically flat
statement: Let R and B be commutative rings with R an integral domain, and let φ : R → B be a finite type ring map [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. There is a nonzero a ∈ R such that, for every B-algebra T that is a localization of B at φ(a) [def-weil-ring-localization-away], the composite R → B → T is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. No Noetherian, finite presentation, or injectivity hypothesis on φ is assumed.

proof.text: The private helper exists_fg_subideal_localized lifts a finite generating set of the kernel ideal localized in a Noetherian ring, clearing denominators. Apply it to P = MvPolynomial (Fin n) R and Q = MvPolynomial (Fin n) (FractionRing R). The private helper exists_finitePresentation_torsion_cover forms the quotient A by that finitely generated subideal. The induced R-algebra map f : A → B is surjective, A is finitely presented over R, and each element of ker f is annihilated by a nonzero element of R. This uses Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial'', the polynomial localization instance, and IsLocalization.algebraMap_mem_map_algebraMap_iff.

The private helper exists_flat_away_of_finitePresentation applies the proved source-library theorem Algebra.FinitePresentation.exists_fg_subalgebra_isPushout to A. The resulting finitely generated integer subalgebra R₀ of R is a Noetherian domain. Apply the proved source-library theorem Module.exists_flat_localizedModule_powers to the descended algebra A₀. IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv transfers module-localization flatness to the ring localization C. Localization commutes with this pushout, using Algebra.isPushout_of_isLocalization and Algebra.IsPushout.comp_iff. Thus base change gives Module.Flat R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R A a)) for the nonzero image a of a₀. Only flatness, not freeness, is required.

For any localization model T of B at φ(a), the map q from C = Localization.Away (algebraMap R A a) to T induced by f is surjective by IsLocalization.Away.map_surjective_iff. Since C is flat over the domain R it is torsion-free: every element of ker f has zero image in C by its nonzero scalar annihilator. IsLocalization.Away.map_injective_iff therefore makes q injective. Its composite with R → C is R → B → T, as checked on elements by IsLocalization.map_eq and f.commutes. Compose the flat map R → C with the bijective, hence flat, map q using RingHom.Flat.comp and RingHom.Flat.of_bijective. This works also for the zero algebra, without a separate case.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_nonzero_flat_localizationAway {R B : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [IsDomain R] (φ : R →+* B) (hφ : φ.FiniteType) :
    ∃ a : R, a ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ (T : Type u) [CommRing T] [Algebra B T]
      [IsLocalization.Away (φ a) T], ((algebraMap B T).comp φ).Flat
